title: Live and fixed imaging of translation sites at single mRNA resolution in the Drosophila embryo
protocol: Set up embryo collection cages.
Collect virgin females homozygous for the nos-scFv-mNG transgene.
Collect males homozygous for the SunTag-hb transgene.
Cross flies to produce embryos with maternally expressed scFv-mNG and zygotically expressed SunTag-hb.
Transfer at least 100 females and 50 males to a collection cage with an apple juice agar plate and yeast paste.
Change the plate on the collection cage to a fresh apple juice agar plate with yeast.
Collect embryos at 25°C for the desired length of time.
Remove the plate after 3 hours of embryo laying.
Age the embryos for 1 hour at 25°C.
Dechorionate the embryos by applying 50% domestic bleach to the plate.
Incubate the embryos with bleach for 2 minutes.
Transfer the embryos to a sieve using water or embryo washing solution.
Wash the embryos thoroughly in the sieve with water or embryo washing solution until no bleach remains.
Transfer the embryos into a glass scintillation vial containing 3 mL fixing buffer.
Add 4 mL heptane and 1 mL formaldehyde to the vial.
Shake the vial at 300 rpm for 20 minutes.
Remove the liquid layer from the bottom of the vial with a plastic Pasteur pipette, taking care not to lose any embryos.
Devitellinize the embryos by adding 8 mL methanol to the glass vial.
Shake the vial vigorously for 30 seconds and vortex for 30 seconds.
Remove the liquid and repeat at least twice more until the liquid is clear with no floating membrane.
Transfer the embryos in methanol to a 1.5 mL eppendorf tube.
Remove as much methanol as possible from the embryos and replace with fresh methanol.
Embryos can then be used for smFISH and immunofluorescence or kept in methanol at -20°C.
Reconstitute the lyophilized SunTag smFISH probes in 400 μL RNase-free TE by pipetting.
Mix to produce a probe stock with a concentration of 12.5 μM.
Make 20 μL aliquots of the dissolved probes.
Store the aliquoted probes at −20°C and protect from light.
Transfer embryos to a glass V-Vial using a pipette with a cut tip.
Wash embryos in 50:50 methanol:PBT for 5 min by rocking.
Repeat washing in PBT three times, each for 10 min by rocking.
Rock embryos in 50% PBT and 50% Stellaris wash buffer for 10 min.
Rock embryos twice in Stellaris wash buffer for 5 min each.
Add 500 μL Stellaris wash buffer to the embryos.
Incubate the embryos with the buffer at 37°C in a water bath for 2 h.
Stain the embryos with SunTag smFISH probes.
Dilute the SunTag probes to a final concentration of 50 nM in 300 μL Stellaris hybridization buffer.
Incubate the embryos in the probe mixture in a 37°C water bath for 12–18 h.
Keep the Stellaris wash and hybridization buffers at 4°C throughout the experiment.
Make fresh Stellaris wash buffer for each experiment.
Cover the V-Vials with foil to maintain darkness after probe hybridization.
Maintain embryos in darkness as much as possible on Day 2.
Pre-warm Stellaris hybridization and wash buffers to 37°C in a water bath.
Wash embryos in Stellaris hybridization buffer for 30 minutes in a 37°C water bath.
Rinse embryos with Stellaris wash buffer.
Wash embryos in Stellaris wash buffer for 15 minutes in a 37°C water bath.
Repeat the previous step twice.
Rock embryos in Stellaris wash buffer for 15 minutes.
Rock embryos three times in PBT for 10 minutes each.
Rock embryos in PBT + 1 × Western Blocking Reagent (WBR) for 30 minutes.
Dilute anti-mNeonGreen antibody at a ratio of 1:250 in PBT + 1 × WBR.
Incubate embryos with the primary antibody solution at 4°C for 12–18 hours.
Rinse embryos with PBT twice on Day 3.
Rock embryos four times in PBT for 15 minutes each.
Rock embryos in PBT + 1 × Western Blocking Reagent (WBR) for 30 minutes.
Dilute anti-mouse AlexaFluor 488 at a ratio of 1:250 in PBT + 1 × WBR.
Incubate embryos with the secondary antibody solution.
Rock embryos in secondary antibody solution for 2 hours at 20°C.
Wash embryos twice with PBT.
Rock embryos in PBT for 15 minutes twice.
Dilute DAPI at a ratio of 1:1000 in PBT.
Rock embryos in DAPI solution for 15 minutes.
Rock embryos in PBT for 15 minutes.
If using ProLong Diamond mountant with DAPI, omit the DAPI incubation step.
Mount embryos on a glass slide.
Remove excess PBT from embryos.
Add approximately three drops of ProLong Diamond to the embryos.
Draw up embryos with a glass pipette and place them onto a glass slide.
Cover the embryos with a Nr 1, 24 mm × 50 mm coverslip using tweezers.
Dry slides for 12–18 hours at 20°C in the dark.
Slides can be stored at -20°C for at least three months without loss of staining.
Image stained embryos using confocal microscopy.
Set up 3 channels for SunTag smFISH, mNeonGreen staining, and DAPI.
Align the anterior-posterior axis diagonally to maximize imaged area.
Use a Leica TCS SP8 AOBS inverted confocal microscope with a 63×/1.40 HCX PL APO CS oil objective and 0.75× optical zoom.
Set white light laser power to 70%.
Configure pinhole to 1 airy unit, scan speed to 400 Hz, line averaging to 2×, and bit depth to 8.
Acquire images at 2048 x 2048 pixels with a pixel size of 0.12 μm x 0.12 μm.
Set z-step size to 300 nm for 107 z-steps, providing an imaging depth of 31.8 μm.
Ensure the z-depth covers from apical to basal fluorescent signals in SunTag smFISH and scFv-mNG channels.
Collect DAPI channel with 405 nm excitation (2%), using a PMT detector collecting from 415 – 470 nm.
Collect scFv-mNG (AlexaFluor 488) channel with 488 nm excitation (10%), using a hybrid detector collecting from 500 – 540 nm.
Collect SunTag smFISH (Quasar 570) channel with 548 nm excitation (15%) using a hybrid detector collecting from 558 – 640 nm.
Ensure the sample slide reaches 20°C before imaging.
Use an objective with magnification sufficient to capture the whole expression domain for whole embryo/expression domain imaging.
Set a laser power for the SunTag smFISH channel that overexposes transcription sites, allowing reliable imaging and detection of individual mRNAs by analysis software.
If analyzing the number of mRNAs within transcription sites, use a lower laser power to prevent overexposure.
Image at least three biological replicates (embryos) as there will be cell-to-cell and embryo-to-embryo variation, especially when analyzing mutant genotypes.
Image a high magnification region of a stained embryo for calculation of ribosome number.
Set the pinhole to 0.65 airy unit.
Set the scan speed to 400 Hz.
Enable 4× line averaging.
Set bit depth to 8.
Acquire an image at 4096 x 4096 pixels.
Ensure a pixel size of 0.009 μm x 0.009 μm.
Use a z-step size of 200 nm for imaging.
Collect the DAPI channel with 405 nm excitation (11%).
Set PMT detector collection from 415 – 470 nm for DAPI.
Collect the scFv-mNG channel with 488 nm excitation (12%).
Use a hybrid detector with collection set from 500 – 540 nm for scFv-mNG.
Gate the scFv-mNG channel at 1–6 μs.
Collect the SunTag smFISH channel with 548 nm excitation (20%).
Set a hybrid detector with collection from 558 – 640 nm for SunTag smFISH.
Gate the SunTag smFISH channel at 1–6 μs.
Ensure no overexposed pixels in the scFv-mNG channel.
(Optional)
Deconvolve images using Huygens Professional Deconvolution Software (SVI).
Load the image into Imaris 9.2.
Create spots in Imaris using the ‘spots’ function to identify mRNAs based on SunTag smFISH signals.
Select the channel used for SunTag smFISH.
Estimate the XY diameter by moving to ‘Slice’ view and measuring the diameter of individual mRNA foci.
Select 'Model PSF-elongation along Z-axis' and 'Background Subtraction'.
Set the 'Filter Type' to 'Intensity Sum Ch=X Img=1', where Channel X is the channel used for SunTag smFISH.
Remove spots with high fluorescence, keeping only those that are low in fluorescence.
Add a filter with ‘Filter Type’ set to ‘Quality’.
Adjust the quality filter until all mRNA spots are selected without excess spots or false positives.
Complete the spots wizard and name the spots 'SunTag mRNA spots'.
Use the Imaris ‘spots’ function to identify potential translation sites based on the scFv-mNG signal.
Select the channel used for scFv-mNG.
Estimate the XY diameter by moving to ‘Slice’ view.
Measure the diameter of individual scFv-mNG foci.
Select ‘Model PSF-elongation along Z-axis’ and ‘Background Subtraction’.
Set the ‘Filter Type’ to ‘Quality’.
Move the filter until all scFv-mNG spots are captured.
Complete the spots wizard.
Name the spots ‘scFv spots’.
Capture all translation sites visually identifiable by colocalization with mRNAs as spots.
Colocalize SunTag mRNA and scFv spots to identify translation sites based on presence of both an smFISH and scFv-mNG signal.
Using the Imaris ‘Surfaces’ function, create surfaces to identify nuclei.
Select the channel used for the nuclear stain.
Set ‘Surfaces Detail’ to 0.5 μm.
Estimate the nuclear size by measuring the diameter of individual nuclei in ‘Slice’ view.
Select ‘Background Subtraction (Local Contrast)’ and set ‘Diameter of largest Sphere which fits into the Object’ as the measured value.
Change the Threshold filter until all nuclei are covered.
Split touching objects by enabling this option.
Set the ‘Seed Points Diameter’ to the measured nuclear diameter.
Set the ‘Filter Type’ to ‘Quality’ and adjust until all nuclei have an object.
Complete the surfaces wizard.
Name the surfaces ‘nuclei’.
Identify mRNAs inside the nucleus.
Check if any translation sites have been assigned inside the nucleus.
Select ‘Suntag mRNA spots’.
Run the Imaris X-tension ‘Split spots into surface objects’.
Select ‘scFv spots co-located’.
Run the Imaris X-tension ‘Split spots into surface objects’.
Export the Imaris data.
Export the ‘SunTag mRNA spots’ data from step 27.
If removal of nuclear mRNAs is required, export the ‘Suntag mRNA spots inside Surfaces’ folder from step 31a.
Export the ‘scFv spots co-located’ data.
If removal of any false positive translation sites is needed, also export the ‘scFv spots co-located inside Surfaces’ folder.
Export the ‘nuclei’ data.
In Anaconda Prompt, type: python.
Drag and drop the spotME_EmbryoMid.py script.
Drag and drop the folder created in step a.
Repeat steps a to c with the ‘scFv spots co-located’ data instead of ‘SunTag mRNA spots’ data.
This will give the data output for translated mRNAs only.
Prepare high magnification images for analysis.
Open the saved Leica image file in Fiji.
Save each channel collected separately as a .tif image.
Name the Suntag smFISH channel as suntag.tif.
Name the mNeonGreen channel as ng.tif.
Open the Airlocalize software.
Select the type of data to be analyzed, here a 3D single image.
Navigate to and select the image that will be analyzed.
Select the mNeonGreen image channel only, named ng.tif.
Determine general analysis parameters in the next window, ‘Quantification Parameters’.
Use default settings in the ‘PSF Width (pix)’ section.
Select an output folder.
Enable the option ‘output image of spots’.
Hover the cursor over the center of a fluorescent signal and left click to verify selection.
Select ‘local gaussian fit’ to display the fit over the fluorescent profile.
Click ‘record fit result’ to provide training data for the algorithm.
Repeat with approximately 10 additional translation sites.
Advance to the next window by selecting ‘done’.
Identify translation sites using a detection threshold.
Modify the threshold until all translation sites are recognized by a red signal overlay on the microscopy image but none of the single proteins are.
Select ‘done’ once the desired threshold is set.
Move analysis files into a subfolder called ‘translation_sites’.
Identify and quantify the fluorescence of single proteins using Airlocalize.
Repeat steps 36a and b to identify single proteins.
Follow steps 36c and d as outlined above or disable the option ‘set manually’ in the ‘PSF Width (pix)’ window.
Modify the PSF values to previously determined values included in the .par3 text file.
Skip step 36d and advance directly to step 36e if disabling the manual setting option is chosen.
Follow steps 36e and f.
Set the threshold so that single proteins are recognized.
Move analysis files into a subfolder called ‘single_proteins’.
Identify and quantify the fluorescence of mRNA molecules for colocalization analysis using Airlocalize.
Follow steps 36a-f as outlined above using the SunTag mRNA microscopy channel.
The input file should be called suntag.tif.
Move the output files into a subfolder called ‘mRNA’.
Perform colocalization analysis and determine the number of ribosomes present in the translation sites.
Open Anaconda prompt.
Type: python.
Drag and drop the folder containing the ribosome_number.py script.
Drag and drop the folder containing the subfolders with the analysis.
The script will identify translation sites by colocalization with mRNA spots, discarding any ‘translation sites’ that do not colocalize.
The script will then take the single proteins and discard any included translation sites.
Calculate the median fluorescence of the remaining single proteins.
Divide the fluorescence of translation sites by this number.
Apply a correction factor to account for ribosomes that have only translated part of the Suntag mRNA sequence.
Calculate the correction factor using (lengthSunTagCDS × 0.5 + lengthhbCDS)/lengthtotal.
Divide the number of ribosomes given in the output file by the calculated correction factor.
Prepare cover slips for live imaging experiments by coating them thinly with heptane glue.
Make a ball of unrolled sellotape and place it in a 50 mL bottle.
Fill the bottle half full of heptane and soak the sellotape for at least 12 h so the glue will dissolve.
Take Nr. 1, 18 x 18 mm coverslips and pipette approximately 60 μL of heptane glue onto the coverslip.
Leave the heptane glue to dry as a thin coating on the slide.
Collect virgin females heterozygous for the scFv-mNG and tdMCP-2xmRuby3-CAAX transgenes and males homozygous for the SunTag-hb-128xMS2 transgene.
Transfer at least 50 females and 25 males to a collection cage with an apple juice agar plate and yeast.
Change the collection cage plate to a new apple juice agar plate with yeast after flies have laid eggs for a desired period.
Let the flies lay for the desired amount of time, then remove the plate for embryo collection.
Dechorionate the embryos by applying 50% domestic bleach to the plate and incubating for 2 min.
Transfer embryos to a sieve by washing them off the plate with water or embryo washing solution.
Wash embryos thoroughly in the sieve with water or embryo washing solution until no bleach remains.
Brush embryos out of the sieve onto an apple juice agar plate under a dissection microscope.
Arrange embryos on the apple juice agar plate using a brush or tweezers so that the imaging area faces upwards.
Mount embryos on a Lumox dish by placing two Nr. 0, 18 × 18 mm cover slips with a small gap of approximately 12 mm in between.
Fill the gap with 70 μL of halocarbon oil (7:1 ratio).
Pick up a heptane glue cover slip and carefully lower it onto the embryos with the glue side down.
Transfer the coverslip with embryos onto the Lumox imaging dish, positioning the embryos within the imaging oil.
Secure the embryo coverslip to the other coverslips on the imaging dish using nail polish.
Set up the microscope with two channels for scFv-mNG and His-RFP, both collecting with Fast Airyscan.
Locate the embryos using brightfield illumination.
Collect a time-lapse movie of a developing embryo for ∼2 h.
Using the His-RFP channel, find an embryo approximately 15 minutes prior to the desired age of imaging.
For imaging translation beginning at nc11, find an embryo where nuclei are just starting to migrate to the surface.
Set up a z-stack including the whole nuclear depth and cytoplasm on either side of the nucleus.
Take a time series with the minimum possible gap between z-stacks until translation has ceased.
Balance speed, resolution, and z-depth of imaging to achieve optimal settings for the experiment.
Use high frame rate to capture dynamics of translation.
Optimize image quality by adjusting imaging parameters if necessary.
Improve time resolution by imaging a smaller region of the embryo or reducing the z-stack.
Image a narrow region of the embryo (∼9 nuclear widths at nuclear cycle 14) extending along ∼30% of the anterior posterior axis.
Achieve a time resolution of ∼40s and an imaging depth of 20.4 μm.
Optimize settings for different microscope or sized section of the embryo if necessary.
Set up the microscope with two channels for scFv-mNG and tdMCP-2xmRuby3-CAAX, both collecting with Fast Airyscan.
Locate embryos using brightfield illumination.
Locate the area where translation is occurring or expected to occur using the objective without zoom.
Zoom into the area so that only a few cells are visible.
Adjust the focus so that the membrane labeled with tdMCP-2xmRuby3-CAAX is in focus.
Identify individual translation sites in mNG if the mRNAs are already being translated.
Acquire a time lapse dataset with a single z plane for the best time resolution.
Focus on the top of the cells where the mRNAs and unbound tdMCP-mRuby3-CAAX proteins show the cell outline prior to nc14.
Once membranes are located, zoom in to image the translation sites.
Balance speed, resolution, and z depth to track single translation sites.
Use a pixel size of 0.09 × 0.09 μm for optimal image quality.
Capture changes associated with translation initiation and elongation at a time resolution of approximately 2 seconds.
Using the Imaris ‘surface’ function, create surfaces to identify nuclei.
Enable ‘Track Surfaces (over Time)’ in the first screen.
Select the Channel used for His-RFP.
Select ‘Enable Smooth’ and set ‘Surfaces Detail’ to 1 μm.
Measure the diameter of nuclei in the ‘Slice’ tab.
Select ‘Background Subtraction’ under Thresholding.
Set ‘Diameter of largest Sphere which fits into the Object’ to the measured value.
Adjust the threshold so that only the nuclei are selected.
Move between frames to check selection consistency across all frames.
Select ‘Enable’ under ‘Split touching Objects (Region Growing)’.
Set ‘Seed Points Diameter’ to the measured value.
Filter seed points by ‘Quality’ to ensure only nuclei are selected.
Use the ‘Number of Voxels Img=1’ filter to eliminate small non-nuclear objects.
In the ‘Tracking’ screen, select the Algorithm as ‘Autoregressive Motion’.
Set Max Distance to 5 μm and Max Gap Size to 3.
Complete the surfaces wizard.
Using the Imaris ‘spots’ function, create spots to identify translation sites.
Deselect ‘Track Spots (over Time)’ in the first screen.
Select the Channel used for ‘scFv-mNG’.
Measure the size of the translation sites in the ‘Slice’ tab.
Enter the value into ‘Estimated XY diameter’ and select ‘Model PSF-elongation along Z-axis’ and ‘Background Subtraction’.
Use filters to select the scFv-mNG foci (translation sites).
Move between frames to check foci are selected in all frames.
Complete the spots wizard.
Export the Imaris data.
Export the statistics in the ‘Statistics’ tab.
Select the desired statistics in ‘Preferences’, which can include the scFv-mNG intensity of each spot and position of the spots in each time point.
Use the Imaris ‘Spots’ function for tracking of translation sites over time.
In the creation wizard, select ‘Track spots over time’.
Select the scFv-mNG channel for analysis and estimate the xy diameter of the translation site.
Using filters, make sure that the translation sites are selected through time.
Select ‘Autoregressive Motion’ for tracking parameters.
Set the ‘Maximum Distance’ parameter to 5 μm.
Set the ‘Max Gap Size’ parameter to 2.
Export analysis files after successful tracking.
In the ‘Statistics’ tab, select ‘Export all Statistics to file’.
Define exported statistics under settings based on analysis requirements.
Include fluorescence intensity quantification in the exported statistics if required.
Include distance and speed of movement in the exported statistics if required.
Perform a background correction for fluorescence intensity quantitation manually.
Place spot objects into different background regions to measure fluorescence value.
Calculate an average background value from the placed spot objects.
Subtract the average background value from the translation site fluorescence.
